notes:
COUNT-VS-ROWS (5-hit pattern, finally checkable on a populated collection): info={page:1,page_size:30,count:14,prev:null,next:null,truncated:false}. count(14) == len(test-results)(14) EXACTLY. page_size(30) > count(14), so no paging was needed or attempted -- this is the one genuinely rich subject in the campaign and its count field is trustworthy. info also carries an undeclared 'truncated:false' key not in the declared info schema (declared required: page/page_size/count/prev/next only).

CONTAINER KEY: guidance explicitly warns 'the list key is test-results with a HYPHEN... this endpoint is the odd one out' -- confirmed correct on the wire; no container-name drift here (unlike the systemic 6-hit pattern elsewhere in the campaign, this capability's own docs already call it out and the API matches).

V1 vs V2 SHARED-DEFECT CHECK (the specific interest for this probe) --
1. result_status siblings: v1 does NOT share v2's defect. All 14 rows here carry the full result_status object (id, field_value, internal_name, field_name, colour, plus value_category) exactly as v1's own schema declares and requires. v2's contract (re-read live via describeCapability just now) has already been corrected in the index to declare result_status as {field_value} only, with guidance text explicitly stating 'id, internal_name, field_name and colour... are deliberately dropped here and never appear' on v2. So this is a genuine, confirmed SERIALIZER DIFFERENCE between the two endpoints for the same field name and the same underlying result rows -- v1's serializer includes the full status object, v2's does not, and both are (now) accurately documented. A caller needing internal_name/id/colour must use v1, not v2, for the same case/run pair.
2. custom_fields type: v1 DOES share the underlying API behavior (returns an empty array, not an object) -- confirmed on all 14 items. However, v1's OWN declared schema still says type 'object' (unlike v2's index entry, which was already corrected to declare 'array'/list-of-entries). So v1 currently carries an UNFIXED version of the same defect v2 had; v2's index was patched, v1's was not. This is worth fixing identically to how v2 was fixed (declare custom_fields as an array here too), or confirming the endpoint really should return an object and treating this as an API bug rather than a docs bug.

NEAR-DUPLICATE QUESTION (get_test_results_for_test_case vs get_test_results_for_test_case_v2) -- read both contracts directly, no invocation of v2 performed (describeCapability only):
- ID FORM: v1 takes project_id as a bare integer, test_case_id as a bare integer (the internal numeric id), and test_run_id as either a bare integer or TR-prefixed string (pattern ^(TR-)?[0-9]+$). v2 requires strict PR-NNN / TR-NNN / TC-NNN identifier strings for all three -- a bare integer either 404s (test_run_id) or fails to resolve (test_case_id, which is looked up by identifier, not the same numeric id v1 uses).
- ENVELOPE: v1's list key is 'test-results' (hyphen); v2's is 'test_results' (underscore). Both capabilities' own guidance text calls this out explicitly and warns a client written against one reads an empty list against the other. Also: v1 nests the response directly with top-level unique_issues; v2 has no unique_issues key at all.
- ROW FIELDS: v1 rows are heavier -- full author object, updated_by object (undeclared but present), backtrace, attachments array, links (self + custom_fields hrefs), full result_status, test_run_step_result. v2 rows are deliberately narrower -- created_by is a plain email string (not an object), no attachments key, no backtrace, no links, cut-down result_status ({field_value} only), but v2 adds fields v1 lacks entirely: test_case_id/test_run_id echoed back as identifiers, execution_id, dataset ([] for non-data-driven runs), urls ({self} undeclared sub-key), and step_result (v2's renamed, still-null-here equivalent of v1's test_run_step_result). configuration_id: v1 declares it but never emits the key at all (declared_missing, confirmed on all 14 rows here); v2 emits it explicitly as null (present-but-null) -- a small but real difference in HOW the same declared-nullable field is absent.
- PAGING: v1's page size is fixed at 30, uncontrollable by the caller (only 'p' is accepted). v2 accepts page_size (or count, which wins if both given) restricted to exactly 30 or 300, giving the caller real control v1 does not offer.
- PREFERRED/DEPRECATED: neither describeCapability response (v1 here, v2 read live for this comparison) carries any preferred or deprecated marker -- no such field appears in either capability's metadata. The routing tie a prior eval hit is real: the index gives no explicit steer between them, and the actual difference is entity-shape/paging/id-form, not one being newer or sanctioned over the other. An agent choosing between them today has to infer id-form and row-richness needs itself.

OTHER CAMPAIGN WATCHPOINTS, checked on this populated item: attachments=[] (empty on all 14, still unverified populated shape), step/test_run_step_result=null on all 14 (still unverified populated shape, all 14 rows are case-level not step-level), dataset is not a field v1 returns at all (v1 has no dataset key; only v2 does), configuration_id is absent as a key on v1 (see declared_missing above) rather than present-and-null as on v2. None of these populated shapes could be exercised here since this run/case pair has no configuration, no dataset, and no step-level results -- consistent with the rest of the campaign's finding that these remain unverified everywhere probed so far.
